narrative: Material PL3__M87AD858 exhibits intermittent demand behavior with high variability (CV=0.61). The demand profile shows 79.8% of working days have non-zero demand, with a mean daily demand of 11385 units. Lead time is unstable (CV=0.67) with an effective lead time of 2.43 days. The current SAP policy with zero safety stock exposes the material to stockout risk. The optimized policy recommends a safety stock of 22,858 units to achieve 95% service level and an order quantity of 114,956 units (constrained by maximum storage capacity of 137815 units). This optimization reduces total annual cost by 60.7% (from $6,106.59 to $2,402.34), primarily through reduced ordering frequency (from 80 to 26 orders per year).
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding - order quantity significantly reduced from EOQ
Lead time is unstable (CV=0.67) - consider supplier performance improvement
Intermittent demand pattern - monitor for regime shifts

research_insights.selected_model: Square-root EOQ with stochastic lead time demand
research_insights.selection_rationale: For intermittent demand with CV=0.61, the classical EOQ model is appropriate as demand occurs frequently enough (79.8% of days) to justify continuous review. Lead time variability (CV=0.67) is incorporated through safety stock based on lead time demand standard deviation. The MOQ constraint of 37,014 units was considered but the EOQ-based quantity of 275,184 units was higher. Storage capacity constraint of 137815 units is the binding constraint, reducing the order quantity from 275,185 to 114,956 units.
research_insights.boundary_risk: HIGH RISK: Order quantity is heavily constrained by storage capacity (114,956 units vs unconstrained 275,185 units). This represents a 58.2% reduction from optimal, increasing ordering costs. Lead time instability (CV=0.67) with transport as the dominant variance component (45.0%) suggests vulnerability to logistics disruptions. Intermittent demand pattern increases forecast uncertainty.
research_insights.escalation_flag: YES - Capacity constraint is binding; consider increasing storage allocation or reducing MOQ
